data.title: Codexis to Participate in Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference
data.description:
REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Codexis, Inc. , a leading provider of enzymatic solutions for efficient and scalable manufacturing of complex therapeutics, today announced the Company will attend the Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference, being held December 1-3, 2026, in New York, New York.

Management will participate in a fireside chat on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 3:00 pm ET. A live webcast of the event will be available in the Investor Relations section of the Company’s website at https://ir.codexis.com. A replay will be archived for 90 days following the event.

About Codexis

Codexis® is a leading provider of high-performance enzymatic solutions for efficient and scalable therapeutics manufacturing. The company is currently developing its proprietary ECO Synthesis® Manufacturing Platform, an aqueous enzymatic process that may offer a scalable alternative to traditional solid phase organic synthesis of oligonucleotide manufacturing. Initially, Codexis is applying its technology to address the rapidly growing demand for RNAi therapeutics. Codexis’ unique enzymes can drive improvements such as higher yields, increased purity, reduced energy usage and waste generation, stereoisomer control of siRNA, and improved overall capacity in manufacturing at substantially lower capital requirements, all of which may lead to greater efficiency and reduced costs. In addition, the company supplies high-performance enzymes through its BioCatalysis business that are used in the manufacture of multiple commercially available small molecule therapeutics. For additional information, please visit https://www.codexis.com.

data.title: Blue Biofuels and Ben Hill Griffin Sign Letter of Intent for King Grass Supply
data.description:
PALM BEACH GARDENS, FL, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blue Biofuels, Inc. OTCQB:BIOF today announced that it has signed a letter of intent with Ben Hill Griffin, Inc. for the long-term supply of king grass to its proposed cellulosic ethanol plant in Frostproof, Florida.

The letter of intent outlines the intent of Ben Hill Griffin to supply and deliver fresh king grass up to 300,000 dry tons annually. This proposed volume is intended to supply a plant designed to produce 25 million gallons of cellulosic ethanol per year and is estimated to require roughly 7,500 acres of cultivation near Frostproof. The proposal contemplates an initial 10-year term with five-year renewal options. Supply commitments would arise upon execution of a definitive purchase agreement; transportation and delivery schedules remain to be negotiated.

A local supply of king grass is central to the Frostproof plant design. Knowing how much feedstock could be available, where it would be grown and how it would reach the plant helps Blue Biofuels assess delivered feedstock costs and gives prospective lenders and investors a clearer basis for evaluating the project.

Quote from CEO

“Reliable availability and close proximity access to locally grown king grass is essential to planning the Frostproof plant,” said Ben Slager, CEO of Blue Biofuels. “Working with Ben Hill Griffin gives us a practical basis for planning acreage, harvests and deliveries as we develop the project. Central Florida has over 300,000 acres of land available to repurpose into king grass cultivation. This would translate to over a billion gallons of biofuels per year.”

About Blue Biofuels Inc

Blue Biofuels is a Florida-based renewable fuels technology company developing its patented Cellulose-to-Sugar (CTS) process to convert plant biomass into sugars for production of renewable fuels, including cellulosic ethanol. Learn more at bluebiofuels.com.

Forward Looking Statements

This release includes forward-looking statements about potential feedstock supply, a definitive supply agreement and commercial facility development. Actual outcomes may differ materially due to financing, agricultural, technical, regulatory and other risks described in the company’s SEC filings.

data.title: 1inch integrates Hyperliquid’s perpetual futures contracts into its dApp and wallet platform
data.description:
1inch (1inch) announced today that Hyperliquid-powered perpetual futures (perps) are now available to users in eligible regions via the 1inch dApp and Wallet.

The DeFi platform said in a press release that by adding perpetual futures, it seeks to strengthen its offerings to make the ecosystem more holistic. Hyperliquid (HYPE) markets are available to dApp and Wallet users on Android, with plans to roll out the 1inch Wallet app on iOS in the "next couple of weeks," according to a 1inch spokesperson.

The statement said that 1inch provides the interface to the markets run by Hyperliquid, which cover crypto, stocks, commodities, and foreign exchange. Users can fund a perps position with a token they already hold on 1inch, which will be routed to USDC and then deposited into a balance on Hyperliquid.

"Our goal is clear: whatever users want to do in DeFi, they should be able to do it through 1inch, while maintaining full control of their assets," said Sergej Kunz, 1inch co-founder.

One of the Hyperliquid perps contracts available on 1inch is ANT, which tracks the anticipated price of one Anthropic Class A share as the AI frontier lab prepares to go public later on Thursday.

The 1inch dApp and Wallet on Android allows users to place a market order, a limit order, or a time-weighted average price (TWAP) order. They can attach a take-profit or a stop-loss at entry, or add one later. Users can also add to a position, reduce it, or close it.

The two apps differ in default margin settings. The 1inch Wallet sets isolated margin as the default so that only the position's margin is at risk. The dApp, on the other hand, sets cross-margin as the default, so the balance on Hyperliquid can back open positions.

Since its launch, major DeFi platforms — including Uniswap, Morpho, and Curve — have integrated Hyperliquid's perps market. Kraken parent Payward is also set to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer of Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets.

According to a recent report from Hyperliquid Research Collective, the derivatives market platform closed out the third quarter with a record $16.8 billion in open derivatives positions, surpassing centralized exchanges such as Bybit, Kraken and OKX in open interest.

data.title: UK CBI industrial orders rebound in November
data.description:
British industrial orders rebounded in November after falling sharply in October, helped by demand from the aerospace and defence sectors, according to a monthly survey from the Confederation of British Industry on Thursday.

The CBI's industrial orders balance rose to a two-month high of -12 in November from a three-month low of -32 in October, while output expectations for the next three months were little changed at +1 in November versus -1 in October.

"After two and a half years of decline, manufacturers are finally seeing some welcome signs of recovery ... but challenges remain, particularly around costs," CBI Senior Economist Cameron Martin said.

  • The export order balance rose to -19 from -25

  • The total order book and export order book were in line with their long-run averages

  • Expectations for average prices over the next three months fell to +20 from October's five-month high of +24

  • The CBI said persistently high energy costs continued to weigh on manufacturers' competitiveness

  • Britain's inclusion in the EU's "Made in Europe" programme remained a pressing concern, the CBI said

data.title: World can manage without Strait of Hormuz, but no return to pre-war normal - IEA
data.description:
The world can manage without the Strait of Hormuz, but it's unlikely that energy markets can return to where they were before the start of the Iran war, according to the International Energy Agency's head Fatih Birol.

"I don't see any credible pathway back to the situation that existed in Feb. 2026," he wrote in an article for The Economist. "Confidence in the strait as a safe and reliable corridor for energy and other goods has been crushed."

As a result, countries will pay more attention to diversification. "They will pursue a more varied mix of fuels and energy technologies, of suppliers and trade routes," Birol stated. "Those new routes will include pipelines out of the Middle East that bypass Hormuz (the UAE and Saudi Arabia are already moving ahead rapidly on these)."

But while the global energy system can diversify away from the strait over time, he insisted the Middle East will remain vital for energy security and markets.

Birol's statements come as the IEA released The World Energy Outlook 2026 on Thursday, which referred to the Strait of Hormuz disruptions as the world's largest energy supply shock.

"At its peak, global oil supply fell by 16M barrels per day and gas supply by 320 million cubic meters per day," it noted.

Its report found that new bypass pipelines, alternative supplies and measures to displace demand could reduce the need for oil flows through the strait from 20 mb/d before the crisis to 8.5 mb/d in 2030 and to under 2 mb/d by 2035.

"But even in this extreme case, the Middle East would remain the world's largest exporter of oil to international markets," the report affirmed.

Notably, Goldman Sachs expects an additional 3.8 mb/d of pipeline capacity to come online over the next year as Middle East oil producers invest in pipelines that bypass the Strait of Hormuz and transport directly to the Gulf of Oman, Red Sea or Mediterranean Sea.

Further to the announcement made on 21 October 2026, Tavistock has now entered an Exclusivity and Option Agreement for the potential sale of Tavistock Group Holdings Limited (the “Disposed Entity”), the owner of Tavistock Private Client Limited (“TPC”), to EPF V UK Wealth Bidco Jersey Limited (the Jersey based holding company for the Atomos group) (“Atomos”) (the “Disposal”).

Exclusivity and Option

This new agreement augments the previous exclusivity agreement with Atomos for which it paid Tavistock £1.5 million (the “Exclusivity Payment”). For a further payment of £100,000 (the “Option Fee”) Atomos now has an exclusive option to acquire the Disposed Entity for an additional cash consideration of up to £27.4 million at any time on or before 31 January 2027 (or such other later date as the parties may agree) (the “Option”).

Background

Atomos and Tavistock have been working together on this transaction since Tavistock accepted a formal offer from Atomos in March 2026. The current situation is that:

  • Atomos is in the process of agreeing terms for W&I cover with the insurer, which has completed its due diligence to date, however, the parties note that the W&I insurer may require refreshed due diligence up to the point of signing. 

The Disposal

100% of the issued share capital of the Disposed Entity will be sold to Atomos for a cash consideration of up to an additional £27.4 million (the “Consideration”) comprising:

  • £18.4 million (a gross payment of £20 million less both the £1.5 million Exclusivity Payment and the £100,000 Option Fee) payable to the Company on completion of the Disposal (“Completion”);
  • an unconditional deferred consideration of £5 million payable twelve months following Completion; and

data.title: Lenzing Shares Struggle Under Heavy Debt — Market Talk
data.description: Lenzing's debt is likely to continue to overshadow the stock next year, analysts at Berenberg caution. The Austrian chemicals group saw net financial debt rise to 1.42 billion euros as of the end of September, up from 1.35 billion at the start of the year, according to an earnings report earlier this month. The company has made progress in cost savings and has been boosted by stronger pricing in some chemical products, Berenberg notes. "[But] the trouble with Lenzing's equity is that the impact of incremental positives on its share price is invariably outweighed by its debt pile," the brokerage says. That will continue to dominate the share in 2027, along with modestly lower pricing for fibers and lower costs for raw materials, Berenberg says. Lenzing shares have lost some 40% year-to-date to trade at around 10.30 euros. ((joshua.kirby@wsj.com; @joshualeokirby))

data.title: Stock Futures Climb Ahead Of Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut — NVDA, BABA, TTWO, SLS Stocks In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its earlier $70 to $78 range, ahead of its Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT.
  • Intel gained more than 4% after securing its first external customer for its 18A chip process and expanding its partnership with Microsoft
  • Palo Alto Networks surged around 10% after beating earnings estimates, while Sellas Life Sciences plunged nearly 18% after a discounted share offering.

U.S. equity futures climbed early on Thursday as investors geared up for Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, above its previously indicated range of $70 to $78.

As of 5.30 a.m. ET, futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.61%, while S&P 500 futures gained 1.15%. Nasdaq-100 futures led the gains, jumping 2.06%.

Earlier, on Wednesday, Wall Street closed mixed, with the Dow losing 1.11% and the S&P 500 slipping 0.23%. The Nasdaq Composite, however, bucked the trend, finishing 0.42% higher.

Oil Prices Edge Higher As Iran War Tensions Persist

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday after falling in the previous session, as growing expectations of a supply surplus and higher interest rates weighed on sentiment, offsetting support from attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran war.

Brent crude futures rose 0.61% to $92.51 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures gained 0.64% to $83.79 as of 5:30 a.m. ET.

The Tech Radar

Intel (INTC): CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company had signed its first external customer for its 18A chip manufacturing process, without revealing the client's identity. Intel sees 18A as an important part of its turnaround strategy. Separately, Microsoft (MSFT) and Intel announced an expansion of their long-standing partnership, including a multi-year agreement to supply Intel Xeon processors to meet growing demand for cloud and AI computing. The developments lifted Intel shares by 4.65% in early premarket trading.

Nvidia (NVDA): President Donald Trump said the U.S. could allow Nvidia to sell its Blackwell AI chips to China in two to three years, provided newer technology is available by then. In an interview with Fox News from Shenzhen, Trump suggested the restrictions could eventually be eased as Nvidia advances to newer chip platforms. Trump's comments followed his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, where access to advanced AI chips was a key point of contention. Nvidia shares rose 2% in early premarket trading.

Alibaba Group Holding (BABA): Shares fell around 0.62% in premarket trading, extending losses after hitting a 22-month low on Wednesday, as investors assessed the impact of tighter U.S. restrictions on advanced AI technology ahead of the company's quarterly results. New U.S. rules restrict overseas data centers from remotely providing large amounts of advanced American chip computing capacity to companies in China and other restricted countries.

Trending Stocks

Palo Alto Networks (PANW): Shares jumped 10.23% in early premarket trading after the cybersecurity company reported better-than-expected third-quarter (Q3) results. CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted a multibillion-dollar opportunity in securing open-weight AI models. During the earnings call, Arora also discussed the company's Applied Compute acquisition, which aims to expand its enterprise AI security capabilities and generate $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by fiscal 2029. The stock is on track for a second consecutive weekly gain.

Take-Two Interactive (TTWO): The developer of Grand Theft Auto VI remained in focus as traders pointed to glowing reviews, strong preorder demand, and streaming buzz behind the stock's rally. Bulls see further upside from the franchise's sales potential, as well as future online and PC releases. The game received a 99/100 score on Metacritic, surpassing GTA V's 97. Take-Two shares were up around 1.27% in premarket trading at the time of writing.

Sellas Life Sciences (SLS): The biotech firm priced its $150 million stock offering at a steep discount, sending shares down 21.23% in early premarket trading on Thursday. The move came a day after investors welcomed positive results from its leukemia trial. Sellas plans to issue around 11.54 million new shares, with the offering expected to close on Friday. Underwriters also have a 30-day option to buy up to an additional 1.73 million shares, which would take gross proceeds to $172.5 million if exercised in full.

What Else To Watch On Thursday

On Thursday, traders will look to weekly jobless claims for fresh clues about the health of the U.S. labor market.

On the earnings front, investors will be watching Walmart’s (WMT) quarterly results for further insight into the health of U.S. consumers. Clothing retailer Gap (GAP), Webull (BULL) and Intuit (INTU) are also scheduled to report earnings.

SPY, QQQ, DIA: Retail Sentiment

Retail sentiment toward both SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500, and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100, remained ‘bullish,’ unchanged in the past 24 hours.

Meanwhile, sentiment for SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) fell to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ during the same period.

Saxon Weald Group (incl. Saxon Weald Capital Plc) – Trading update for the six months ending 30 September 2026

Saxon Weald Group is today issuing its consolidated trading update for the six months ended 30 September 2026. These figures are unaudited and for information purposes only. Highlights for the period ending 30 September 2026:

  • Saxon Weald owns and manages 7,064 homes;
  • Turnover for the period was £32.7m (September 2025: £29.2m); 
  • Social housing lettings turnover contributed 91% of total turnover (September 2025: 96%); 
  • Operating surplus (including asset sales) for the period was £9.5m (September 2025: £10.6m); 
  • Operating margin on social housing lettings was 26% (September 2025: 29%); 
  • Overall operating margin (including asset sales) was 29% (September 2025: 36%); 
  • Overall operating margin (excluding asset sales) was 28% (September 2025: 30%); 
  • Net margin on shared ownership (first tranche) was 15% (September 2025: -);
  • The surplus after tax for the period was £2.5m (September 2025: £3.9m); 
  • Debt ratio was 53% (September 2025: 51%); and 
  • Return on capital employed for the period was 2.1% (September 2025: 2.4%).

Commenting on the results, Rachel McGoff, Executive Director of Finance & Governance, said:

During the first six months of 2026/27, Saxon Weald has focused on delivering the ambitions set out in our new three-year Corporate Plan, Delivering Better Together, while maintaining our focus on financial resilience and delivering safe, high-quality homes for our customers.

We have continued to strengthen our understanding of the condition of our homes with stock condition survey coverage exceeding 80% by the end of September, on track to meet our target of 90% by the end of 2026/27. This improved data is giving us a stronger evidence base for investment decisions and supporting our longer-term plans for the quality, safety and sustainability of our homes.

We have also continued to invest in energy efficiency. By the end of September, 67% of our homes met our target EPC standard, up from 61%, with grant funding secured to continue our programme of works over the remainder of the year.

Customer satisfaction has remained strong, averaging 83.3% in the six months to September 2026, compared with 84% at the end of 2025/26. We continue to focus on improving the quality, responsiveness and accessibility of our services.

Our transformation programme has moved into its next phase, bringing together improvements to services, processes, data and technology. During the period, we continued to embed our new customer contact capability and progressed plans to improve our processes, data and systems, with the aim of creating simpler, more responsive services for customers and more efficient ways of working for colleagues.

Alongside investment in existing homes, we have continued to deliver new affordable housing. We completed 55 new homes by the end of September and have a steady future delivery pipeline that balances the need for new affordable homes with investment in our existing homes and our long-term financial resilience.

data.title: Palo Alto’s AI Ambitions Come With A Catch — Why Morningstar Calls PANW’s $4.5B Deal 'Risky'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Palo Alto’s first-quarter sales rose 39% year-over-year to $3.44 billion, beating the $3.31 billion consensus estimate.
  • Morningstar assigned Palo Alto a “Very High” Uncertainty Rating, citing rapid technological change and disruption from smaller rivals.
  • Jefferies raised its price target to $450 from $400, saying “AI tailwinds starting to emerge.”

Palo Alto Networks' (PANW) proposed $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute could put the cybersecurity company in competition with frontier artificial intelligence (AI) research labs, according to Morningstar, which described the deal as “risky.”

Morningstar called the acquisition “distinctly non-cybersecurity” in nature, but said it could let Palo Alto train AI models tailored to cybersecurity while reducing its dependence on frontier research labs.

“We see this deal as risky,” Morningstar senior equity analyst Malik Ahmed Khan wrote, adding that since the company will be post-training open models, a widening gulf between the frontier and open models would put Palo Alto at a “slight disadvantage.”

At the time of this writing, stocktwits.com/symbol/PANWPANW stock was up over 9% in the premarket session, on track to extend the previous session’s nearly 10% gains.

AI Security Demand To Drive Growth

The note comes after Palo Alto reported first-quarter earnings on Wednesday, with sales up 39% year-over-year to $3.44 billion, beating the $3.31 billion consensus estimate tracked by Fiscal.ai.

Despite its concerns about the acquisition, Morningstar remains positive about Palo Alto's position in AI-related cybersecurity spending. It views the company as a cybersecurity leader, with platforms spanning network security, cloud security, identity, and security operations.

“We believe the firm stands to materially benefit from secular tailwinds across its three key end markets as cloud migrations, the shift to zero-trust security, and increased automation in cybersecurity increase Palo Alto’s value proposition to its clients,” the Morningstar note said.

According to the analyst, Palo Alto’s sticky platforms, combined with the broad range of its cybersecurity solutions, have helped the company build a “wide economic moat around its business”.

PANW Valuation And Risks

Morningstar retained its $300 fair value estimate for PANW stock despite the company's strong quarterly performance, implying a potential downside of nearly 12% from the last closing price of $339.9 per share.

The research firm continues to favor Palo Alto's positioning in AI-related security spending and cybersecurity vendor consolidation. However, it assigned a “Very High” Uncertainty Rating, citing rapid technological change and potential disruption from smaller cybersecurity rivals.

The firm warned that “an inaccurate assessment of future customer demand could lead Palo Alto to either overpay in an acquisition or overspend to develop the same technology in-house.” It also flagged talent shortages and data privacy and security as potential risks.

Meanwhile, Jefferies raised its price target on the stock to $450 from $400 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, citing another material acceleration in fiscal first-quarter core net new annual recurring revenue, driven by AI and observability tailwinds, according to TheFly.

The firm described the results as “another clean print,” with “AI tailwinds starting to emerge”. Jefferies’ target implies a potential upside of 32%.

What Retail Thinks About PANW Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around PANW stock flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ a day ago amid ‘extremely high’ user message volume. The stock was among the top-trending tickers on the platform.

So far this year, PANW stock has surged over 89%. In comparison, the First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR) and the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG), which hold Palo Alto shares, have risen over 35% and 56%, respectively, over the same period.

data.title: Lenovo Maintains Revenue Momentum on AI-Fueled Hardware Demand — Update
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Lenovo Group reported robust sales in the fiscal second quarter, on track to achieve its $100 billion annual revenue goal thanks to strong artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand.

Surging demand for AI servers and enterprise infrastructure has enabled the world's largest personal-computer maker to achieve better-than-expected results recently, offsetting a broader downturn in global PC shipments.

The company on Thursday said revenue for the three months ended September jumped 48% from a year earlier to $30.24 billion, beating market expectations.

Its adjusted net profit more than doubled to $1.36 billion, higher than analysts' estimate of $1.27 billion in a Visible Alpha poll. However, its bottom line was hit by a noncash fair-value loss arising from the revaluation of warrants, resulting in net loss of $640 million.

The company's infrastructure-solutions business, encompassing data-center hardware like AI servers, remained the biggest earnings driver. Segment revenue more than doubled from a year earlier.

In addition to cloud service providers, AI adoption by enterprises and small and medium businesses is accelerating. Their revenue surged 200% in the last quarter, outpacing the 170% growth of cloud-service providers.

Lenovo has been leveraging demand in the U.S., where the largest market opportunity for infrastructure currently resides. But that could also present challenges for its AI infrastructure business, especially after some cloud-service providers faced severe financial distress and Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections.

Chief Executive Yang Yuanqing downplayed these concerns in an interview, highlighting broadening AI-related demand. AI computing is moving beyond a handful of cloud service providers, increasingly being used by businesses and starting to be integrated into personal devices, he said.

Other headwinds are also at play as the industry deals with a memory crunch and rising consumer-electronics prices, though Lenovo has handled them relatively well. Its intelligent-devices group, which includes PCs, smartphones and tablets, recorded 15% revenue growth in the latest quarter.

That came as global PC shipments fell 20% in July to September, according to industry tracker IDC. Continued supply constraints and the inventory rush ahead of memory-chip-driven price hikes left the quarter with little demand to draw on.

Lenovo remained the world's largest PC maker by shipments during the quarter, with a 23.8% market share.

Next year, component costs could remain at current elevated levels, if not higher, Yang said. But thanks to the company's strategic shift toward premium products, the devices segment should be able to maintain flat or single-digit revenue growth, he said.

data.title: Investec Likely to See Slight Upgrades as Consensus Follows Guidance — Market Talk
data.description: Investec can expect slight upgrades as consensus on fiscal 2027 largely captures management's guidance, J.P. Morgan analyst Baron Nkomo says. Although the financial-services company's first-half results are positive--with adjusted EPS growth of 7.4% ahead of expectations--JPM stays neutral on the shares as it sees greater upside in other South African banks. The company offers reasonable EPS growth and a good return on equity, Nkomo says. The London-listed company is backed by a liquid, well-funded, and strongly capitalized balance sheet and well-positioned to drive profitable growth in specialist banking while scaling high-margin, capital-light businesses, the analyst adds. "We see resilient operating momentum, but near-term operating leverage remains constrained by elevated investment." Shares are down 7.5% at 554.50 pence. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)

data.title: Rupee hits 7-month high at 93.33 against dollar as FPI buying, softer oil prices boost recovery
data.description:
The Indian rupee extended its winning streak on Thursday, November 19, reaching a seven-month high against the US dollar as continued foreign investor purchases and easing crude oil prices provided support to the domestic currency.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee strengthened to 93.3340 against the dollar, compared with its previous close of 93.4175, marking an appreciation of 7.75 paise.

The domestic currency began the session at 93.4000 and fluctuated between 93.1700 and 93.5500 during the day.

The recent appreciation has been driven by consistent foreign portfolio investor (FPI) participation in Indian equities, relatively cheaper crude oil and traders reducing their bearish positions on the rupee. However, a firm US dollar and the possibility of additional monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve remain potential headwinds.

What is driving the rupee's recovery?

  • Continued buying by foreign investors

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) maintained their positive stance on Indian equities for a 13th consecutive trading session on Wednesday. According to provisional exchange figures, they bought shares worth ₹5,866.78 crore.

These investments have contributed to higher dollar availability in the domestic foreign exchange market, providing support to the rupee.

  • Easing crude oil prices

Movements in international oil prices remain an important factor for the Indian currency, given the country's dependence on crude imports.

Brent crude, the global benchmark, was trading 0.26% lower at $91.71 per barrel in futures trade.

A moderation in oil prices can lower India's overall import expenditure and reduce the dollar requirement of domestic oil importers. This, in turn, eases demand for the US currency and provides some relief to the rupee.

  • Traders reduce bearish positions

Changes in currency market positioning have also helped the rupee gain ground. Market participants have been cutting back on bets against the Indian currency, triggering short-covering activity.

This reduction in bearish positions has added to the buying support for the rupee and contributed to its recent appreciation.

  • RBI initiatives and changing market positions

Measures introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), including initiatives to encourage foreign currency deposits, have also been identified by market strategists as factors supporting the domestic currency.

Additionally, the reduction of speculative long positions in the US dollar has helped ease pressure on the rupee.

What could limit further gains?

Despite its recent advance, the rupee continues to face risks from international monetary developments. The US dollar has remained relatively strong, with the dollar index trading close to a 19-month high.

Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting highlighted policymakers' concerns about persistent inflation. Some officials indicated support for additional monetary tightening.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller has also proposed a 50-basis-point interest rate increase in December or a quicker pace of hikes in 2027.

Higher interest rates in the US could make dollar-denominated assets more attractive to global investors, potentially strengthening the greenback and restricting further gains in the Indian currency.

data.title: German Stocks Rise On Tech Boost; DAX Up 0.23%
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - German stocks gained some ground in positive territory Thursday morning, after posting losses in the previous three sessions. Tech stocks found support after Anthropic's IPO raised a record $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX's reported $75 billion offering.

The benchmark DAX, which climbed to 25,945.59 earlier in the day, was up 60.17 points or 0.23% at 25,817.00 a little over half an hour before noon.

Infineon Technologies climbed nearly 3.5%. Deutsche Bank, MTU Aero Engines, Siemens Energy and Hochtief gained 2%-2.5%.

Siemens moved up nearly 2% and Daimler Truck Holding advanced 1.8%. Commerzbank gained about 1.1% after the German government reached an agreement with UniCredit on the takeover of the lender.

BASF, Bayer, Brenntag, Heidelberg Materials, Gea Group, Continental, Merck, Adidas and Siemens Healthineers posted modest gains.

SAP drifted lower 2.1%. Henkel shed nearly 2%. Fresenius Medical Care and Rheinmetall lost 1.4% and 1.2%, respectivelyl. Vonovia, Hannover RE, Munich RE, Deutsche Boerse, Beiersdorf and Symrise lost 0.7%-1%.

In economic news, the euro area current account surplus remained unchanged in September, data from the European Central Bank showed. The current account logged a surplus of EUR 12 billion in September, broadly unchanged from the previous month.

The surplus on goods trade fell to EUR 14 billion from EUR 21 billion. Meanwhile, the services surplus rose to EUR 16 billion from EUR 13 billion.

In the twelve months to September, the current account surplus declined to EUR 248 billion from EUR 279 billion a year earlier. The surplus was equivalent to 1.5 percent of euro area GDP.
